meta.title: Co-ops of Whatcom County
meta.description: Every co-op we could verify in Whatcom County, coloured by kind, with the documented ties between them. Lines are only ties with a public source — every line's popup says what the tie is and where it came from. Absence of a line means no tie was found, not that none exists. Two Skagit organisations (NABC and Puget Sound Food Hub, Mount Vernon) are included because they built Whatcom-serving co-ops; zoom out to see them. Not mapped: Bellingham housing co-ops (a Bellingham Housing Co-op Resource Center exists, but the names that surfaced online — Pacific Heights, Eight Oaks and others — appear to be British Columbia co-ops, and no Bellingham address could be confirmed); the Nooksack Tool Co-op (forming 2016–19, status and location unknown); Organic Valley member dairies (no local site). Main source: Cascade Cooperatives' Whatcom & Skagit co-op map. Researched Sep 2026 by Marc Pierson with Claude Opus 5.5.

develop.label: Built or helped build the co-op

parcels.label: Cascade Cooperatives
parcels.notes: Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, incorporated 2019. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer.

parcels.label: Community to Community (C2C)
parcels.notes: 203 W Holly St #311, Bellingham. Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén. Food-sovereignty and farmworker organisation; develops farmworker co-ops. foodjustice.org · (360) 738-0893.

parcels.label: NW Cooperative Development Center — local staff
parcels.notes: Based in Olympia; Bellingham support staff (local contact Deborah Craig). Supports new co-ops and conversions, especially home-care co-ops. Pin location approximate. nwcdc.coop · (360) 943-4241.

parcels.label: NW Agriculture Business Center (Mt Vernon)
parcels.notes: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 419 S 1st St #207, Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre. Shown because it built two Whatcom-serving producer co-ops.

parcels.label: A1DesignBuild
parcels.notes: 3310 Northwest Ave, Bellingham. Design/build firm dating to 1955 (roots 1928); converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Bellingham Bay Builders
parcels.notes: 2111 King St, Bellingham. Worker co-op builder founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents
parcels.notes: Worker-owned mountain-guiding collective, founded 2023. Various locations — pin is in the Mt Baker foothills. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Cooperative
parcels.notes: 1155 N State St #508, Bellingham. Founded 2009 — oldest and largest home-care co-op in Washington. In-home care for elders and disabled people. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Community Media Cooperative
parcels.notes: Worker co-op established 2023. Location varies — pin approximate. media-coop.com. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad
parcels.notes: 1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.

parcels.label: Yellow Cab Co-op
parcels.notes: 401 Harris Ave (Fairhaven Station), Bellingham. Employee-owned since August 2023, taking over Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (founded 1992). 24-hour dispatch, all of Whatcom. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation
parcels.notes: 4202 Meridian St #105, Bellingham. Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Community Food Co-op
parcels.notes: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Industrial Credit Union
parcels.notes: Main branch 1100 N State St, Bellingham; also Sunset, Northwest Ave, Bakerview, Ferndale, Lynden, Nugents Corner. Founded 1941. Absorbed Ferndale Refinery Credit Union in 2012. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: North Coast Credit Union
parcels.notes: 1100 Dupont St, Bellingham; also Northwest Ave and Ferndale (plus Skagit branches). Founded 1939. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: WECU
parcels.notes: 600 E Holly St, Bellingham; also Ferndale and Lynden. Founded 1936 as Whatcom Educational Credit Union. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: WestEdge Credit Union
parcels.notes: 2501 James St, Bellingham. Founded 1953. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: REI Bellingham
parcels.notes: 400 36th St, Bellingham. National consumer co-op (1938); Bellingham store opened 1999.

parcels.label: North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative
parcels.notes: PO Box 244, Acme; farm stand at 2399 Mt Baker Hwy. Farmer-owned (Whatcom and Skagit ranchers), established 2016 (organising from 2012). USDA-inspected mobile slaughter. Founding board: Buttin' Grove Farm, Matheson Farms, Hannegan Farm and Home. Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: Darigold — Lynden plant
parcels.notes: 8424 Depot Rd, Lynden. Dairy farmers' co-op (~250 member farms, 4 states). Its predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in 1918. About 95% of Whatcom dairies ship to Darigold. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

parcels.label: CHS Northwest (was Whatcom Farmers Co-op)
parcels.notes: 415 Depot Rd, Lynden (Farm & Home); also 300 Main St. Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS — the national farmer-owned co-op — and now trades as CHS Northwest: farm supply, energy, agronomy for Whatcom and Skagit. Sits beside the Darigold plant; zoom in to separate the two pins.

parcels.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (Mt Vernon)
parcels.notes: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 15612 Best Rd, Mount Vernon. Farmer-owned; serves Whatcom through King counties, with a Whatcom aggregation drop at Cloud Mountain Farm Center, Everson. Cascade Cooperatives member.

links.label: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund
links.notes: The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history.

links.label: Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers
links.notes: Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.

links.label: Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising
links.notes: C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.

links.label: Supplies produce
links.notes: The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.

links.label: Supplies grass-fed beef
links.notes: The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.

links.label: Co-op development help (USDA grant)
links.notes: Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell membership and equity shares. Source: agbizcenter.org.

links.label: Incubated the food hub
links.notes: NABC ran the hub until it incorporated as a farmer-owned co-op in 2016 and governance passed to its own board.

links.label: Home-care co-op support
links.notes: NWCDC lists Circle of Life among the Washington home-care co-ops it serves. Its role in the 2009 founding is not documented.
